injuries.description: C4-5 disc space slightly narrowed, with minimal posterior bulging and loss of lordotic curvature
source: The cervical MRI showed that C4-5 disc space was slightly narrowed, with minimal posterior bulging and loss of lordotic curvature.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

injuries.description: facet hypertrophy at L3/4, L4/5 and L5/S1; mild disc protrusions at L4/5, L5/S1 and S1/2 and annular tear at S1/2
source: Lumbar MRI showed that facet hypertrophy at L3/4, L4/5 and L5/S1 level was pre-existing and degenerative in origin. MRI also showed relative mild disc protrusions at L4/5, L5/S1 and S1/2 levels and the annular tear at S1/2.
injuries.icd_description: Certain specified injuries of abdomen, lower back or pelvis

injuries.description: increased psychiatric symptoms and Post Traumatic Stress Disorder symptoms in the form of nightmares of the Accident; minor residual psychiatric symptoms
source: Dr Lai noted that the plaintiff was mentally stable prior to the Accident in May 2014 and diagnosed that she suffered increased psychiatric symptoms and Post Traumatic Stress Disorder symptoms in the form of nightmares of the Accident and she was likely suffering from minor residual psychiatric symptoms.

manifestations.description: severe neck pain and back pain
tenderness on the back of her neck and her lower back
decrease in range of movement of neck and back
numbness over right upper and lower limbs
limitation of range of movement of back
back pain when bending down or raising hands; difficulty in carrying heavy objects and having prolonged standing, walking and sitting
anxiety, depression, insomnia, nightmares and flashback of the Accident

treatments_received.treatment: Ambulance to Accident and Emergency Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital; admitted and discharged same day
source: Shortly after the Accident, the plaintiff was taken by ambulance to the Accident and Emergency Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital. She complained of severe neck pain and back pain. She was found to have tenderness on the back of her neck and her lower back and abrasion wound on right knee. She was admitted to the hospital for treatment and discharged on the same day.

treatments_received.treatment: Soft neck collar, analgesics and a week of antibiotics; cervical MRI
source: After discharge from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital on 16 May 2014, the plaintiff went to the Hong Kong Sanatorium and Hospital on the same day. She was found to have mild occipital and neck tenderness and was given a soft neck collar, analgesics and a week of antibiotics. MRI of cervical spine was done on 19 May 2014 which revealed minimal posterior bulging of C3-4 disc without fracture or cord injury. She was advised to wear soft neck collar for 3 days and take oral and topical analgesics. Sick leave was granted from 16 May 2014 to 18 May 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: Physiotherapy (neck care, mobilisation, stretching, stabilisation exercises, hot pack); two courses with some attended sessions and defaults
source: The plaintiff started physiotherapy treatment on 17 October 2014. She complained of neck and low back pain as well as decrease in range of movement of her neck and back. Neck care, mobilization and stretching exercises for her neck, back care, mobilization, stretching and stabilization exercises, passive mobilization and hot pack to back were included in the rehabilitation programme. She completed 5 sessions but defaulted 6 sessions. She was last seen on 16 December 2014 and defaulted thereafter. She started another programme on 12 May 2015. She complained of right side low back pain, decrease in range of movement of back. Back care, mobilization, stretching and stabilization exercise were provided. She attended 4 sessions but defaulted 3 sessions.

treatments_received.treatment: Occupational therapy / vocational counselling; work rehabilitation service and recommendation for work hardening
source: On 22 January 2015, the plaintiff first attended the Occupational Therapy Department of the Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital for work rehabilitation service. She complained of tenderness over her neck, right shoulder and back at movement, as well as numbness over right upper and lower limbs. Vocational counselling was provided but it was noted that she was unemployed for the last 2 years. She was suggested to try a part-time home helper job which was referred by the Social Welfare Department. The work capacity demonstrated during the assessment did not match the demands of home helper due to her fair right hand endurance to cope with cleaning and lifting tasks. She was recommended to try a course of work hardening. Home exercise of neck and back was suggested.

treatments_received.treatment: Psychiatric consultation and pharmacotherapy (public psychiatric clinic); increased psychiatric medication after Accident
source: She was first seen at Western Psychiatric Center in December 2004 and was diagnosed to have panic disorder. She was treated with antidepressant and her mental state was stabilized. ... After the Accident, when attending a consultation on 29 May 2014, the plaintiff said that she was anxious, felt short of breath and had recurrent nightmare of the Accident.

treatments_future.treatment: Continue treatment in public psychiatric clinic once in 6 to 8 weeks
source: Dr Lai advised that the plaintiff could continue treatment in public psychiatric clinic once in 6 to 8 weeks and the cost per session was about $200.

treatments_future.treatment: Possibly another 6 months of psychiatric treatment (opinion of Dr Lai)
source: It was likely that she required another 6 months of psychiatric treatment.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: because of the injuries suffered as a result of the Accident, she was unable to do the household chores like cleaning the toilet and kitchen, wiping and mopping the floor, washing, ironing, grocery shopping, cooking, cleaning the furniture and the windows etc. and needed a part-time domestic helper to help her.
